title: Automatic updates — what you will see

steps.path: The version chip at the bottom of the window, once an update has downloaded
steps.headline: Once the new version has downloaded by itself, the chip says it is ready instead of available. Same yellow pulse.
steps.changed: "v1.4.0 — Update available" becomes "v1.4.0 ready — restart to update". The tint and the pulse stay, as you picked.
steps.notice: You know the update is already on your computer, and that a restart (or just quitting later) is all it takes.
steps.risk: While it is still downloading, the chip keeps saying "Update available", so for a few minutes after a release it reads as it does today.

steps.headline: The popup says the update is ready and when it will install, and Restart to update replaces Update now.
steps.changed: Title "Update ready", with one line under it: "Downloaded. Installs by itself the next time you quit YouCoded." The button reads "Restart to update: v1.3.2 → v1.4.0". The Updates card gains "Install updates automatically" under Get beta builds.
steps.notice: Doing nothing is fine: it installs on its own when you next quit. The button is only for getting it right now.
steps.risk: Nothing new to learn, but someone who never quits YouCoded (laptop always asleep, never closed) only gets updates when they press the button.

steps.path: Click the version chip, on a computer where installing needs a password (Linux package installs, a Mac account that is not an administrator)
steps.headline: Where installing needs a password, the line under the title says the button will ask for it, and quitting does not install.
steps.changed: The line reads "Downloaded. Restarting asks for your password, then installs it." Everything else matches the step before.
steps.notice: No password box ever pops up while you are closing the app; it only appears after you press Restart to update.
steps.risk: On these computers the update waits until someone presses the button, so they can fall behind if nobody opens the popup.

steps.path: Click the version chip after turning Install updates automatically off
steps.headline: With the switch off, the line under the title stops promising an install on quit.
steps.changed: It reads "Downloaded. Restart when you are ready." and changes the moment you flip the switch below it. The switch's own description is now "Downloads new versions by itself. Off: you choose when to update."
steps.notice: The popup never tells you something that your switch has turned off.
steps.risk: An update that had already downloaded before you turned the switch off stays ready; turning it off stops the next ones, not this one.

steps.path: Press Restart to update while conversations are open
steps.headline: Restart to update shows the same close-window prompt as quitting, worded for a restart. Closing it with the ✕ cancels the restart.
steps.changed: Same prompt and Resume on Next Launch switch you already know. Only three words change: the title "Restart to update", "Restarting will end your active sessions", and the red button "Restart" instead of "Close window".
steps.notice: You can still ask for your conversations to come back after the restart, exactly as when you quit.
steps.risk: You asked for "the standard closeout prompt"; the wording change is mine, so a button saying "Restart" does not read as quitting for good. Say no to keep "Close window" word for word.

steps.path: Settings → Help & feedback, scrolled to the bottom
steps.headline: Install updates automatically sits right under Get beta builds, in the Help build YouCoded group.
steps.changed: One new row with the same look as Get beta builds: a circular-arrows icon, "Downloads new versions by itself", and a switch that starts on.
steps.notice: Turning it off here or in the update popup is the same setting; each shows the other's change.
steps.risk: The group is named Help build YouCoded, which fits beta builds better than automatic updates.

steps.path: Settings → Help & feedback, the last group
steps.headline: Should the two update switches get their own group in Help & feedback?
steps.today: Get beta builds sits in the group "Help build YouCoded", under Contribute to YouCoded. The new switch went right beside it, as you asked.
steps.problem: The tester looked for the update switch and found it last, after scrolling, under a heading about contributing. Automatic updates have nothing to do with helping build the app.
steps.proposal: Keep both switches together, but decide which heading they sit under.

options.label: A new "Updates" group
options.summary: Contribute stays alone under Help build YouCoded; a new last group, Updates, holds Get beta builds and Install updates automatically — the same name the update popup already uses for them.
pros: The heading says what the switches are.
Same name as in the update popup, so both places match.
cons: One more heading in the popup.
Get beta builds moves from where it is today.

options.label: Keep them under Help build YouCoded
cons: The automatic-updates switch sits under a heading about contributing.
